perspective:
From Keith’s available perspective:

- Keith works with Elizabeth at a construction company; she is the receptionist, and they have a friendly but professional relationship through his office visits for paperwork/project updates.
- Recently, Keith observed Elizabeth being unusually curt/short with him over several days.
- He wondered whether he had upset her, possibly through a misunderstanding or an unknown mistake.
- He asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her. He heard her say no, not at all; she was dealing with personal stuff and apologized if she seemed short.
- Keith felt sympathetic and wanted to support her.
- He offered to listen and suggested a coffee break. Elizabeth accepted and thanked him.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses; Keith perceived them as quite severe.
- Keith suggested she consider talking to a professional, saying an outside perspective can sometimes help. Elizabeth said she had thought about it but was unsure/hesitant about seeking help.
- Afterward, Keith noticed Elizabeth become slightly withdrawn. He thought his suggestion might have embarrassed her and felt regretful.
- He told her he hoped he had not overstepped and that he wanted her to know he was there to support her no matter what. Elizabeth said he had not overstepped, appreciated his concern, and said it was a lot to think about.
- Following that conversation, Keith observed Elizabeth seeming more open and appreciative. He believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him. He intended to maintain the supportive relationship.
- He told her he was glad they talked and that he is always available if she needs to chat or take a break. Elizabeth thanked him, said it meant a lot, and said she felt better knowing she had his support.

Keith does not have access to Elizabeth’s private thoughts, hidden events, or details about her stress beyond what she directly told him or what he observed.
